# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Lower Back Disc Surgery/Decompression (CPT 63030)

**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W530749089
**Denial date:** 2026-07-31
**Reference number:** POC-F7C299C469-49918
**Payer/Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois

**Governing policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026)
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), noticed on 2026-07-31. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision in light of its own coverage policy and the records already in my file.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

Cigna's own policy, CMM-606, sets out the criteria for when an initial lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary. The policy states:

> "Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy or Hemilaminectomy) CMM.SP.IN.606.2 v1.0.2026 Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

One of the qualifying conditions listed involves symptom-and-position criteria, along with a threshold for insufficient improvement despite exam findings. The policy states:

> "▪ symptoms worsen with standing and/or walking ▪ symptoms are alleviated with sitting and/or forward flexion • Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

and further:

> "◦ positive straight leg raise ◦ positive crossed straight leg raise ◦ positive femoral stretch test ◦ dermatomal sensory deficit ◦ functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness) ◦ reflex changes ◦ unremitting radicular pain into the lower extremity(ies) without concordant objective exam findings • Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

My medical records document the following, which I believe correspond to these criteria:

- **Symptom duration and functional limitation:** I have had 14 months of progressive lower back pain unrelieved by rest, and the record documents that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes because of pain, along with radicular pain radiating into my right calf.
- **Imaging:** An MRI of my lumbar spine on 2026-06-08 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Exam findings:** My chart documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging.
- **Failed conservative care:** I completed 12 weeks (16 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

Cigna's policy also states that lumbar microdiscectomy is not medically necessary if it is performed "without meeting the criteria in the General Guidelines... and the criteria in the applicable procedure-specific section," or for certain "sole indications" that do not by themselves establish medical necessity:

> "Non-Indications CMM.SP.NI.606.
